findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.comment: The person in charge (PIC) was unable to provide disinfection procedures in the case of vomit or diarrhea. CORRECTED- the CDC Norovirus procedure handout was given to the PIC, and bleach is available. Ensure directions are made readily available in order to properly disinfect in the case of a vomit or diarrhea incident.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee don gloves without prior hand washing. CORRECTED- education regarding times to wash hands was conducted. Instances where hand washing is required includes (but is not limited to): before donning gloves, after touching a personal electronic device, after using cleaning products, when switching between raw and ready to eat foods. Review times to wash hands with all food handlers to ensure proper employee hygiene.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.[P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector verified the process of moving foods from the grill to the concessions. The Certified Food Protection Manager stated that foods are brought from the grill to concessions with no covering. Cease this practice. Cover foods with a lid or foil between buildings to prevent the contamination of foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed liquid cheese and cooked hamburgers to have internal temperatures of 112F and 128F respectively. CORRECTED- the temperature of the hot holding units were increased, and the foods were observed above 135F. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are held at or above 135F to prevent the growth of pathogens. If TCS foods are out of temperature, time as control (food is to be used or discarded within 4 hours) should be implemented.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The hot holding units holding liquid cheese and cooked meats were holding foods below 135F (see violation #22). CORRECTED- the temperature of the units was increased, so that foods were observed above 135F. Ensure all hot holding units are set so that TCS foods have an internal temperature above 135F (in the case of hot foods, cold foods must be kept at or below 41F).
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Multiple boxes housing single service containers were observed on the floor in both the main concessions area, as well as in the 3rd base concessions/ storage area. Discussed with the PIC. Ensure all foods and food contact surfaces are stored 6 inches or more above the ground to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed spoons at the main concessions stand in a mixed orientation. CORRECTED- the spoons were rearranged with a gloved hand so that all handles are facing outward. Ensure single service utensils are arranged so that the food contact and hand contact surfaces are separate to prevent potential bare hand contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Where to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste. 

Multiple employees are observed to wash their hands in the three part sink in the main concession stand. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that proper hand washing procedures are enforced at the facility. Food handlers should only wash their hands in the designated hand washing sinks.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand sink in the third base concession stand is without paper towels on inspector arrival. The PIC was notified and supplied paper towels to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times to promote correct hand washing.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used.

1) Plastic spoons are observed at the stand alone ice cream stand in a cup with the handles and food/lip contact surfaces intermixed and exposed. The PIC was shown and instructed to arrange them so that the handles are up/exposed to correct. (REPEAT) 2) Food boats are observed throughout the the main concession stand with the food contact surfaces up/exposed. Education was conducted and the stacks of boats flipped over to correct. Ensure that all single service items are protected from contamination prior to use/service.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a sanitizer ready for use in the facility. Buckets were made during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizers are available and ready for use at al times that foods are being handled in the facility.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

Facility did not have a form of verification for responsibility to report during this inspection. Inspector gave copies of the SCDPH reporting agreements. PIC is instructed to have all food employees sign copies and to maintain the copies for future inspections.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hand to turn off the faucet. PIC was consulted and education took place. They are instructed to review hand washing and enusre that proper procedures are followed in the facility.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

On arrival, the steam well used for hot holding of cooked burgers and hot dogs is observed to not be holding foods at correct hot holding limits. Items were observed between 85F-96F internal temperatures. Per the PIC the items were cooked approximately half an hour prior to observation. These items will be used or discarded within 4 hours. The steam well does not appear to be turned on. It was activated and was observed at correct temperatures later in the inspection.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Pork chops, brots and hot dogs are observed sitting out to thaw by the grills. Education was conducted as to the safe ways to thaw TCS foods. It was suggested that instead of two freezers, it may be better to have a freezer and a cooler at this location. Inspector also suggested thawing under refrigeration in the walk in cooler across the walkway. Brots are observed still frozen at this time. PIC indicated that the other items had been sitting for less than half an hour  when observed. All items were moved back into the freezers to correct.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent. 

The screen door for the concession stand does not have a self closer correctly installed and does not fully close easily. PIC is instructed to ensure that a self closer is correctly installed at this location. PIC indicated that this will have to go through the park district. Ensure correction prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

1) Cardboard boats are observed stored with the package open and the food contact surfaces facing up. 2) To-go containers are observed out of their packaging and with the eating surfaces up. PIC was consulted and the items adjusted to correct the violation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

The hand sink in the concession stand is observed pulling away from the wall. PIC was consulted and instructed to repair (caulking suggested) prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employees washed hands without using a barrier to turn the faucet off. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC. Use a barrier to prevent recontamination of clean hands. Ref. 2-301.12 [P]
Employees donned gloves without washing hands first. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC and staff. Wash hands before donning gloves. Ref. 2-301.14 [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: No sanitizer bucket prepared at beginning of inspection despite food prep occurring. CORRECTED-- Discussed w/ PIC who made sanitizer bucket. Have sanitizer prepared any time food is being prepared or served. Ref. 4-303.11 [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Handsink is not caulked to the wall. Repair/caulk to eliminate gap between sink and wall. Ref. 6-201.17 [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-305.11 (B) (C) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

1) Phones were observed stored next to the popcorn machine. 2) A woman's clutch was observed on the cleaned dishes in storage. Both items were moved to a container stored under and away from food and food contact surfaces.
